lede: Bitcoin has slumped to around $62,000–63,500, its lowest since July, after roughly $2bn of leveraged longs were liquidated over the weekend as markets brace for a December Fed hike. Forex and gold are closed: gold ended the week down about 4.6% at $3,883 and EUR/USD near 1.1023, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.15%.

focus.text: Ended the week at $3,883, down about 4.6%, as 5%+ yields and Fed-hike bets weighed; opens Monday below its $3,891.6 pivot. US retail sales (Tue) and FOMC minutes (Wed) are next.
Closed at 1.1023, down about 1.1% on the week and below its 1.1039 pivot, with the dollar index at a 19-month high. US retail sales on Tuesday is the first test.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) ≈ 34 on H4 · below 50-day (~4,154) and 100-day (~4,196) SMAs · MACD below zero
technicals.note: Gold keeps printing lower highs and lower lows since the 11 Nov high near 4,066; Friday's rebound from the 3,852 yearly low stalled around the 3,900 area.

technicals.indicators: Stochastic deeply oversold (≈6–14) · MACD below zero and its signal line · price on the lower Bollinger band
technicals.note: The pair extends a sequence of lower highs from the August reversal near 1.1700 and closed the week under the 1.1044 support flagged by analysts.

technicals.indicators: Below 20-day SMA (≈1.3358) · MACD below signal line and zero
technicals.note: Sterling shed almost three cents from last week's 1.35 high and is resting on the 1.32 handle, with October's lows near 1.3140 below.

technicals.indicators: Below 200-day MA (~73k) and 200-week MA (~67.8k) · Fear & Greed 10–15 (extreme fear) · 7-day change ≈ -16%
technicals.note: Saturday's slide broke Friday's ~67,550 low and the 200-week average, leaving the July 2026 lows as the next chart reference below 60,000.

technicals.indicators: Daily RSI in oversold territory · below 200-day EMA (~2,300) · MACD below signal
technicals.note: Ether lost the 1,850–1,930 band and touched ~1,711, its lowest since early July, extending a sequence of lower highs since October.

news.text: Governor Waller floated a 50bp December hike after a 0.3% core CPI print, and Dallas Fed's Logan wants at least two more quarter-point moves; futures fully price a 25bp hike.
The 10-year Treasury yield ended the week near 5.15%, up roughly 27–30bp, its sharpest weekly rise since April 2025.
Brent closed the week at $95.84, a second weekly drop, as escorted Gulf exports resume while the White House keeps a 'status quo' stance on Iran.
The S&P 500 gained about 2.5% on the week despite Nvidia's ~13% slide after Jensen Huang's surprise resignation; Nvidia reports on Tuesday.
Semafor reports White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett is expected to step down.
Bitcoin briefly hit about $62,100 in Asia on Sunday, its weakest since mid-July and roughly 25% below its late-October level; it is down about 16% in seven days.
About $2bn of positions were wiped out in 24 hours per CoinGlass, including $774m in BTC and $488m in ETH, overwhelmingly longs; Binance saw nearly $800m.
US spot bitcoin ETFs bled about $1.07bn over 9–13 Nov, with outflows every day; ether ETFs lost roughly $394m.
BNB fell below $600 for the first time since August, about 23% lower than before the 29 Oct Binance hack despite full customer reimbursement.
Bitcoin mining difficulty dropped 9.1% on Saturday, the largest downward adjustment since June.
Solana slid over 12% toward $69 as its Breakpoint conference opens in London (15–17 Nov); Starknet unlocks 127m STRK today and Arbitrum 92.65m ARB on Monday.

upcoming.note: Prev +0.3% q/q; feeds the BoJ December hike debate.
Exp +0.2% m/m after +0.8%; control group exp +0.4%.
First report under interim CEO Colette Kress; key for AI stocks and US indices.
Gauge of appetite for a 25bp vs 50bp December hike.
Media reports trading could start Thursday; timing not officially confirmed.

weekly_summary.summary: A hot October CPI and hawkish Fed speakers pushed markets to fully price a December rate hike, sending the 10-year Treasury yield up about 27–30bp to 5.15% and the dollar index to a 19-month high. Gold suffered its tenth weekly loss in twelve and EUR/USD and GBP/USD both fell about 1%. US stocks still rose as chipmakers rallied, even as Nvidia sank on its CEO's exit. Crypto had its worst week in months, with bitcoin losing about 16% amid heavy ETF outflows and a weekend liquidation wave.

performance.note: Higher real yields and hike bets; 10th weekly drop in 12
Fed out-hiking ECB; four straight daily losses
Broad dollar strength; rests on 1.32 handle

Second weekly drop; IEA flags surplus
7-day change to Sun ≈07:00 TRT; ETF outflows, liquidations

top_stories.text: October CPI rose 0.4% (core 0.3%) and PPI's annual rate hit 6.5%, cementing December hike expectations.
Waller, Logan, Collins and Hammack all leaned hawkish; Waller said a 50bp move should be considered.
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO with immediate effect; CFO Colette Kress is interim chief and the stock lost about 13% on the week.
Gold briefly fell to about $3,852, a one-year low, and silver dipped below $50 before recovering slightly on Friday.
Bitcoin broke below its 200-day and 200-week averages as spot ETFs posted five straight outflow days and liquidations topped $2bn.
